# The GOCOSMO* knobs are reported by go env, both in the listing and by
# name. A consumer probes GOCOSMOPLATFORMS to tell a toolchain that honors
# the platform selection from one that ignores it, so the probe is
# load-bearing outside this repo: keep it working.

# Unset: every platform the toolchain can emit boot support for.
go env GOCOSMOPLATFORMS
stdout '^linux/amd64,linux/arm64,darwin/amd64,darwin/arm64,windows/amd64$'

# Set: the effective selection, in canonical order, not the raw string.
env GOCOSMOPLATFORMS=windows/amd64,linux/amd64
go env GOCOSMOPLATFORMS
stdout '^linux/amd64,windows/amd64$'

# An unknown platform is refused by name, with the accepted ones listed.
env GOCOSMOPLATFORMS=linux/riscv64
! go env GOCOSMOPLATFORMS
stderr 'unknown platform "linux/riscv64"'
stderr 'darwin/arm64'

env GOCOSMOPLATFORMS=

# The other three cosmo knobs report their effective values too.
go env GOCOSMOFAT GOCOSMOSTRIP GOCOSMODEBUG
stdout '^on\non\nfull$'

env GOCOSMOFAT=0
env GOCOSMOSTRIP=off
env GOCOSMODEBUG=slim
go env GOCOSMOFAT GOCOSMOSTRIP GOCOSMODEBUG
stdout '^off\noff\nslim$'

# A one-architecture selection means no fat build, whatever GOCOSMOFAT says.
env GOCOSMOFAT=
env GOCOSMOPLATFORMS=linux/amd64,windows/amd64
go env GOCOSMOFAT
stdout '^off$'

env GOCOSMODEBUG=
env GOCOSMOSTRIP=
env GOCOSMOPLATFORMS=

# All four appear in the plain listing.
go env
stdout GOCOSMODEBUG=
stdout GOCOSMOFAT=
stdout GOCOSMOPLATFORMS=
stdout GOCOSMOSTRIP=
